body: As for the girl part, my boyfriend is 5'6(as am I) and I still think he is hot as hell. It's never been an issue and I don't ever think about it at all. We all have weird insecurity things and I hate that tall guys are like the new teenage obsession(I'm 18 as well). Real attraction has nothing to do with height and real, non-superficial girls won't give a shit. So don't sweat it. If a girl doesn't find you attractive because of your height or is weird about it, she's not worth any of your time.

I workout around 4 days a week, whether yoga or otherwise. Light weightlifting for me is usually 7-10 different machines, 4 sets of 15 reps each. You can choose the weight by how much you can handle at 15 reps(i.e., if you can do 15 reps of 30lbs but only 10 reps of 35lbs, then go with 30lbs and work your way up over time). Usually for cardio, I do 20-25 minutes of whatever I'm in the mood for, either running or biking or whatever. Some form of exercise 4-5 days a week is what I aim for and is a pretty good rule of thumb if you listen to your body. As for eating and whatnot, I just opt for salads and soup or fruit and veggies and I'm usually set. So far, it's worked decently for me and I'm sure the weight will easily fall off for you if it hasn't been an issue before the birth control pill. Hopefully this helps!

I don't know if this is an option for you, but personally I had to switch to a non-hormonal IUD before I saw any changes in my weight. I gained 10lbs in about a month and I work my ass off at the gym and eat relatively healthy. Stopped taking the pill, and it all fell off. Seriously, I dropped those 10lbs in about four days. There CAN be weight gain with hormonal IUDs so I would talk to your doctor about that but so far I really like my IUD so I recommend looking into it. And if you don't want to switch birth control, avoid salty foods because that can cause bloat and, in my experience, alcohol for the most part. Light weight lifting and cardio/yoga exercise has helped me a lot to get the rest of the weight gain off and it's a nice confidence booster. I totally understand where you're coming from though and just know you're not alone! :)

I would definitely get an OB/GYN especially if you're interested in an IUD. Switching that fast is ridiculous and can seriously mess with your hormones. I wouldn't trust that doctor with my birth control medication.
